m1l1.q: What does a JS engine do first with program text?
m1l1.explain: First the lexer (scanner) turns the character stream into a list of tokens. Only then does the parser build the AST from them.

m1l1.q: Put the engine pipeline stages in order.
m1l1.explain: Source → lexer → tokens → parser → AST → compiler → bytecode → virtual machine → result.
The parser reads tokens and builds an abstract syntax tree (AST).

m1l1.q: Which engine powers Chrome and Node.js?
m1l1.explain: V8: Chrome and Node.js. SpiderMonkey: Firefox. JavaScriptCore: Safari. Hermes: React Native.

m1l2.q: What tokens will the lexer produce for this code?
m1l2.explain: 7 tokens: keyword, identifier, operator, number, operator, number, semicolon.
Inside quotes it's just text: a string token. The lexer recognizes it from the opening " character.

m1l2.q: How many tokens (excluding EOF) does this expression have?
m1l2.explain: a, >=, 10. The lexer uses maximal munch, so >= is one token, not > and =.

m1l2.q: What does our lexer do with whitespace and // comments?
m1l2.explain: Spaces and comments only separate tokens. The lexer skips them. (Real JS remembers newlines for ASI.)

m1l3.q: What will this snippet add for input 123+4 (i = 0)?
m1l3.explain: The loop consumes digits until +. slice(0, 3) is "123".

m1l3.q: Why check operators longest-first: === before == before =?
m1l3.explain: Maximal munch: if = were first, === would be eaten as three separate = tokens.

m1l3.q: How many tokens (excluding EOF) will the lexer emit?

m2l1.q: What node is the root of every AST in our engine?
m2l1.explain: Program holds a list of statements (body). Same as ESTree.

m2l1.q: What is the root of this expression?
m2l1.explain: * binds tighter, so 2 * 3 becomes the right child of +. The root is +.

m2l1.q: Put the nodes on the path from root to the number 1.

m2l2.q: Operator ** is right-associative. What is the result?
m2l2.explain: 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512. In a Pratt parser: parse the right side with bp − 1.

m2l2.q: In a Pratt parser: when does an operator "take" the left expression?
m2l2.explain: Loop: while (bp(op) > minBp) { … }. That one line handles all precedence.
options: When it appears first in the file

m2l2.q: How should this expression be grouped?
m2l2.explain: Subtraction is left-associative: (10 − 4) − 3 = 3. Otherwise you'd get 9.

m2l3.q: What node will this code produce?
m2l3.explain: IfStatement has test, consequent (then branch), and alternate (else branch).
After let the parser expects an identifier. That's a syntax error, caught before anything runs.
You can assign to an Identifier (or property), not to a BinaryExpression.
options: Left side of = must be an assignment target

m3l1.explain: evaluate(node) looks at node.type and recursively evaluates children. Simple, but slower than bytecode.

m3l1.q: When will b() NOT be called?
m3l1.explain: Short-circuit: LogicalExpression evaluates the right side only when it must.

m3l2.explain: A block creates a new environment. Inner x disappears after leaving the block.

m3l2.q: How does the interpreter look up a variable?
m3l2.explain: Environment chain: env → env.parent → … → global. Missing? ReferenceError.
The environment remembers which names are const and blocks assignment at runtime.

m3l3.explain: The inner function keeps a reference to the environment with n. Each call increments the same n.

m3l3.q: What does a function object (closure) store in our engine?
m3l3.explain: new Closure(node, env). On call we create a new Env whose parent is the captured env.

m4l1.q: Put the bytecode for the expression in order.
m4l1.explain: Push both operands first, then ADD pops two and pushes the result.

m4l1.q: What value remains on top of the stack?
Why bytecode instead of walking the AST?
m4l1.explain: Less pointer chasing, better CPU cache, easier optimizations. V8 has the Ignition interpreter.
options: A flat instruction list runs faster
Because you can't execute an AST

m4l2.q: What instruction does the compiler emit for an if condition?
m4l2.explain: Evaluate test → JUMP_IF_FALSE past the then branch. With else, add JUMP at end of then past else.

m4l2.q: Put the loop compilation outline in order.
m4l2.explain: Test at top, conditional jump to end, body and unconditional jump back to test.

m5l1.q: Which objects does mark & sweep remove?
m5l1.explain: Roots: globals, stack, registers. Anything unreachable from roots is garbage.

m5l1.q: Put the GC phases in order.
m5l1.explain: Mark: traverse graph from roots. Sweep: free everything without a mark.

m5l1.q: Why can't reference counting handle cycle a ↔ b?
m5l1.explain: a holds b, b holds a. Even if nothing else sees them, both have count 1.

m5l2.explain: That's why the young generation is collected often and cheaply, and the old one rarely.
options: Old objects are removed most often

m5l2.q: What algorithm does V8 use for the young generation?
m5l2.explain: Live objects are copied to the other semi-space half. Dead ones vanish for free.

m6l1.q: When do two objects share a hidden class (shape)?
m6l1.explain: {x, y} and {y, x} are different shapes. Initialize fields in a consistent order.
options: Same properties added in the same order

m6l1.q: An inline cache speeds up obj.x because…
m6l1.explain: Same shape? Read straight from the remembered offset, without a name lookup.
options: It remembers shape and offset from the last access

m6l2.q: Order V8 execution tiers from simplest.
m6l2.explain: Ignition: bytecode interpreter. Sparkplug: fast baseline. Maglev: mid-tier optimizer. TurboFan: strongest.
JIT assumed x is always a number. A string showed up? Fall back to slower, safe code.
options: When JIT assumptions (e.g. types) stop holding
